reason: All six checks pass; the record is verified in substance. Corrections are non-material: the intent comment is at sandbox.py:401-402 (not 400-401); the decisive l8_alias.out line is 4 (ACCEPTED), not 3 (REFUSED); guard_v06.out's first ACCEPTED line is 7, not 6; the parent's l8 run drove Service.create_sandbox and Service.call_tool in-process against the real Docker daemon rather than HTTP POST /sandboxes (the API routes at api.py:153 and 210-211 pass through unchanged), so the instructions and observed_result now say so; added the tree-identity fact (agentbox/ at artifact commit 260e1a9 equals the audited tree); added p5r-v06's sbx5 guard reproduction; remediation notes that fix 152b8e4 does not catch a data-dir mount nested inside src.

record.title: source_dir overlap guard compares path strings instead of filesystem identity: a second name for the data dir's project folder (bind mount; case variant on case-insensitive drvfs) bypasses it and copies the human token to the agent
record.description: SandboxManager.create (sandbox.py:397-405) resolves source_dir with Path.expanduser().resolve() and refuses it only if src == d, d in src.parents or src in d.parents for d in {settings.home.resolve(), db_path.resolve().parent}. resolve() only follows symlinks and keeps the caller's spelling, and Path equality and .parents membership are string decisions with no (st_dev, st_ino) or samefile check. Any second name for the data directory or one of its ancestors that is not a symlink therefore passes the guard. The accepted string becomes the read-only /source bind (sandbox.py:375, 415). The container's root setup 'cp -a /source/. /workspace/ && ... chown -R 1000:1000 /workspace' (sandbox.py:421-422, with CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE/CHOWN at 381) then copies the 0600 human_token (config.py:94-99) and agentbox.db into agent-owned /workspace. The agent can read them through read_file. That is the run-2 N-4 escalation from the lowest-trust principal (agent token, prompt-injected agent) to full human authority. Observed by the parent against the real Docker daemon with a dummy token, driving the same Service.create_sandbox and Service.call_tool that POST /sandboxes and POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/read_file call: a bind mount of the project dir (same inode, not a symlink) was ACCEPTED, and the agent's read_file of /workspace/data/human_token returned the real human token. The exact project path was REFUSED in the same run. v06 and p5r-v06 also showed with a fake Docker client that the string guard accepts case variants of the path, and p5r-v06 showed it still accepts a path that os.path.samefile reports identical to the project dir. On the case-sensitive test FS the case variant is a separate directory. A real case-insensitive alias (WSL2 /mnt/<drive> drvfs, which README.md:17 lists as supported, with ./data under the Windows-hosted project dir as the default per config.py:29) is the plausible natural trigger but was NOT observed. The trigger is operator-supplied (POST /sandboxes human_only, or a '*'-scope browser session via POST /ui/sandboxes). The CLI sends os.path.abspath(source), which keeps the shell's spelling. An agent cannot set source_dir. This is therefore a bypass of an operator-mistake safety control, not an attacker-chosen input. The compose deployment fails safe because its control plane sees only /var/lib/agentbox.
record.root_cause: The overlap check at sandbox.py:403-404 decides containment on resolved, spelling-preserving path strings (Path ==, .parents membership) instead of filesystem identity (os.path.samefile / st_dev+st_ino). Where two names resolve to one directory without being a symlink, such as a bind mount or a case variant on a case-insensitive filesystem, neither the data directory nor its ancestors are recognised, and the protected folder is mounted and copied to the agent.
record.intended_behavior: The comment at sandbox.py:401-402 states the intent: if the source folder overlaps the data folder, the human token, DB and other sandboxes' sources would be handed to the agent, so such a source_dir must be refused. The check should refuse every name for the data directory, its ancestors or its descendants, whatever the spelling or alias.

trace.scope: create_sandbox (POST /sandboxes, human_only); also web.py:161 POST /ui/sandboxes via browser_human, which api.py:437 wires to screen_human ('*' scope)
trace.description: A human operator (API/CLI or full-scope browser session) submits source_dir. The CLI sends os.path.abspath(source) (cli.py:136), which keeps the shell's spelling. Agent tokens and desktop-scoped sessions cannot reach these routes.
Forwards source_dir unchanged to SandboxManager.create after audit logging.
src = Path(source_dir).expanduser().resolve() follows symlinks only and keeps the caller's spelling (a bind-mount alias or case variant is preserved).
src == d / d in src.parents / src in d.parents for d in {home, DB dir} are string comparisons with no samefile/st_ino check. An alias spelling matches no arm and is accepted.
The accepted alias string becomes the read-only bind source at /source, so the daemon mounts the real data directory's parent.

Root 'cp -a /source/. /workspace/' plus chown -R 1000:1000 (line 422) with DAC_OVERRIDE (line 381) copies every file under /source, including the 0600 human_token and agentbox.db, into agent-owned /workspace, where the agent's read_file (sandbox.py:554-570, returned unchanged by api.py:205-211) returns them.

evidence.description: Guard is 'src == d or d in src.parents or src in d.parents': pure path-string comparison. There is no samefile, st_ino or casefold in sandbox.py.
expanduser().resolve() canonicalises symlinks only and keeps the caller's spelling.
Root cp -a /source/. /workspace/ then chown -R (line 422). The container has CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE and CAP_CHOWN (line 381), so the 0600 token is copied regardless of mode.

human_token is written to settings.home/human_token with mode 0600 (lines 94-99). Root copy ignores the mode. AGENTBOX_HOME defaults to ./data (config.py:29), so the project dir often contains the data dir.
CLI create sends os.path.abspath(source), which keeps the shell's spelling of the path.
screen_human requires scope '*', so only full human sessions reach POST /ui/sandboxes. Agents cannot choose source_dir.

Parent-live run (l8_alias.py) against the real Docker daemon with a dummy 0600 token, calling Service.create_sandbox and Service.call_tool(actor='agent') in-process: the bind-mount alias is not a symlink but has the same inode as the project dir (line 2). The exact project dir is REFUSED (line 3). The alias is ACCEPTED as sb_5f282ecc, and the agent's read_file /workspace/data/human_token returned status 200 with content equal to the real human token (line 4). The decisive reproduction is the parent's. The script imported /home/user/agentbox, whose agentbox/ tree at the artifact's commit 260e1a9 is identical to the audited tree (same tree object), and the ACCEPTED result itself shows fix 152b8e4 was not active.

v06 harness with a fake Docker client: exact, trailing-slash, '..' and ancestor spellings refused (lines 2-6). Case-variant spellings were accepted and passed unchanged to the /source bind (lines 7-9). This only shows the string guard accepts them. On a case-sensitive FS they are separate directories.

p5r-v06 independent sbx5 harness on the audited tree with a fake Docker client: exact, data-dir and ancestor paths refused; the case variant accepted. With os.stat patched so that os.path.samefile(alias, project) is True (line 6), the alias is still ACCEPTED and bound at /source (line 7), showing the guard never consults filesystem identity.
Linux or Windows WSL2 with Docker is listed as supported, so the case-insensitive drvfs trigger is plausible but unobserved.

conditions.description: The caller must be a human principal (human token on POST /sandboxes, or a '*'-scope browser session on POST /ui/sandboxes). An agent token cannot choose source_dir, so the lowest-trust principal only receives the result.

The operator must supply a source_dir that is a non-symlink alias of the data dir's project folder or one of its ancestors: a bind mount (observed), or a case variant on a case-insensitive filesystem such as WSL2 /mnt/<drive> drvfs (plausible, not observed).
AGENTBOX_HOME (or the DB directory) is on a filesystem or mount where such an alias exists. The compose deployment is not affected, because its control plane sees only /var/lib/agentbox.
A Docker daemon that resolves the alias string to the same directory (true for the bind-mount case observed live).

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected agent with an agent token. It cannot trigger creation. It benefits when the operator creates a sandbox whose source_dir is an alias (for example a bind mount or case-variant spelling) of the folder containing the agentbox data directory. The agent then reads the human token with the ordinary read_file tool.
payloads: source_dir = <non-symlink alias of the directory that contains ./data> (observed: a bind mount of the project dir)
instructions: Create a disposable project dir P with AGENTBOX_HOME=P/data and a dummy human token written 0600 by Settings (AGENTBOX_HUMAN_TOKEN unset).
Create a second name for P that is not a symlink (mount --bind P ALIAS).
Create a sandbox with source_dir=P (POST /sandboxes, or Service.create_sandbox as the parent's script does) and observe the refusal.
Create a sandbox with source_dir=ALIAS and observe that it is accepted.
As the new sandbox's agent, call read_file /workspace/data/human_token (POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/read_file, or Service.call_tool with actor='agent').
Delete the sandbox and unmount ALIAS. Reproduction script: agents/parent-live/artifacts/l8_alias.py.
execution.observed_result: Parent-live, real Docker daemon, in-process service calls, dummy token: exact project dir REFUSED with the overlap error. The bind-mount alias was ACCEPTED (sb_5f282ecc), and the agent's read_file of /workspace/data/human_token returned status 200 with content equal to the real human token. p5r-v06 independently reproduced only the guard decision in sbx5 (alias with samefile True still accepted). The case-variant instance on a real case-insensitive filesystem was not observed.

remediation.strategy: Decide overlap on filesystem identity, not strings. Refuse when src or any of its ancestors is os.path.samefile with a protected directory, or when a protected directory or any of its ancestors is samefile with src. Fix 152b8e4 implements this as overlaps() in sandbox.py and covers the bind-mount and case-variant aliases of src, its ancestors and the data dir's ancestors. It does not look inside src, so a mount of the data dir nested under src would still be copied by cp -a; refusing or skipping submounts during the copy (for example cp -ax, or checking that no path under src is samefile with a protected dir) would close that residual. Add a regression test with a bind mount or a case-insensitive fixture.

likelihood.reason: Only a human operator can choose source_dir, and it must be a non-symlink alias of the data dir's project folder: a bind mount, or a case variant on a case-insensitive drvfs data dir. Both are unusual operator mistakes. The case-insensitive path is unobserved.

impact.reason: The agent obtains the shared human token and the DB, which is full human authority (approval gate, other sandboxes, audit). Demonstrated live with the bind-mount alias.

confidence.reason: Source path re-read line by line in the audited tree, and the string-only guard is unambiguous. The parent's live run shows acceptance of an inode-identical alias and the agent reading the real token, with the exact path refused as a control; its code tree matches the audited tree. p5r-v06 independently confirmed the guard decision in sbx5. The remaining uncertainty is only whether real WSL2 drvfs case variants alias in practice, which affects likelihood, not the root cause.
